## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-fascicle Sòng-dynasty sub-commentary by [普觀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%AE%E8%A7%80) on [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F)'s [KR6n0091](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0091) *Dàshèng fǎjiè wú chābié lùn shū* (T44n1838) — the Tang Hua-yan-school commentary on Sāramati's *Dharmadhātu-aviśeṣa-śāstra* ([KR6n0089](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0089)). The companion *kē* (topical outline) is [KR6n0092](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0092) (X46n0786). Pǔguān's pair of works is one of the principal Sòng-period engagements with the Tathāgatagarbha treatises in Chinese Buddhist scholarship.

**Abstract**

The Sòng dynasty saw a partial revival of Hua-yan-school doctrinal scholarship after the late-Tang persecutions and the dispersal of the Tang Hua-yan-school institutional base. Pǔguān's sub-commentary belongs to this revival: it engages with [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F)'s text not merely as historical doctrine but as living philosophical resource, applying Sòng-period scholastic methods (the *kē* + *chāo* paired format) to the *Dharmadhātu-aviśeṣa* tradition. The work is one of the few Sòng-dynasty sub-commentaries on the Tathāgatagarbha treatises (most Sòng Buddhist scholastic energy went into the Tian-tai and Chán traditions), and is a valuable witness to the continued Hua-yan-school doctrinal interest in the post-Tang period.

The dating window adopted (1100–1180) follows the conventional floruit for Pǔguān; specific composition dates are not preserved in the colophon. Pǔguān's other principal surviving work is the [KR6i0368](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0368) *Lánpén jīng shū huìgǔ tōngjīn jì* 蘭盆經疏會古通今記, also a sub-commentary in the *kē + jì* format.
